remaining_untested_explanations: projection capacity changes together with dynamic input access; no parameter-matched comparison
optimization under alternative training settings or a retuned configuration
forecast boundary behavior: last context row rather than last observed values; initial missing zeros are fed with masks set to one
missingness representation, including the absence of an explicit elapsed-time channel
unchanged recurrent-state/coupling handling in the admissible-edge architecture
separate CinC-2012 seed behavior is outside this CinC-2019 control
interpretation: Giving every no-edge organ node all 16 dynamic variables and their masks lowers renal pooled RMSE in 4/4 paired seeds on both splits: the seed mean changes from 0.846332 to 0.712003 on A (shared − partitioned -0.134330) and from 1.067043 to 0.939610 on B (-0.127433). This is a one-factor input-scope control at a fixed selected configuration, not a retuned model. Both context and forecast-step inputs are widened, while both arms retain no edges, organ-specific output heads, static inputs, and the same forecast boundary/mask rules; shared forecast feedback carries the preceding predictions of all organs. The comparison also widens projection capacity (759952 versus 778384 parameters), so it does not distinguish input access from that capacity change. The unresolved alternatives named in RENAL_DIAGNOSIS.md remain optimization, forecast boundary handling, and missingness representation, including the lack of explicit elapsed-time inputs; recurrent-state/coupling handling is unchanged. This comparison does not resolve the frozen admissible-edge architecture or the separate CinC-2012 seed behavior. It reports direction and magnitude for these saved fits.
